title: Secretary Bessent IMFC-DC Statement
summary: Treasury Secretary Bessent delivered the US statement at the IMF-World Bank Spring Meetings on April 15, 2026, calling for institutional reform at both the IMF and World Bank to refocus on core mandates. The statement emphasized reversing IMF "mission creep" into development, climate, and social issues; advocated for stronger program conditionality and debt sustainability analysis; and criticized the World Bank's 45% climate finance target as inefficient and mission-distorting. The US reiterated commitment to IMF quota-based governance and the 16th General Review of Quotas.
key_points: US calls for IMF to reverse "mission creep" and focus surveillance on external sector imbalances, cross-border spillovers, and industrial policies affecting domestic demand
IMF lending should emphasize policy conditionality addressing root causes of BoP problems, credible macro projections, and rigorous debt sustainability analysis
US expects IMF to emphasize outcomes over financing volume through Review of Program Design and Conditionality
US supports the 16th General Review of Quotas to reinforce IMF's quota-based status; future quota realignment requires a new quota formula
US calls on World Bank to eliminate 45% climate finance target, stating it "breeds inefficiency, distorts economic decision making, and moves the Bank away from its core mission"
US advocates for robust implementation of IBRD Graduation Policy to redirect resources to poorest, least creditworthy countries
US calls on IFC to meet 2018 capital increase pledge of 40% of new commitments in poorest/most fragile countries

macro_context: The statement reflects US G20 priorities for a "more balanced global economy" and emphasizes promoting domestic revenue mobilization and private sector-led growth in borrower countries. The focus on external sector imbalances and industrial policies aligns with the US stance on addressing trade imbalances. However, the statement provides no specific macro data or forward guidance on US monetary or fiscal policy.
